newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran naval forces parade in biggest Gulf wargames.
newsitem.headline: Iran naval forces parade in biggest Gulf wargames.

text.p: Naval forces of Iran's elite Revolutionary Guards paraded before the Islamic Republic's supreme leader at the entrance to the Gulf on Wednesday in the country's largest ever wargames.
Frigates, fast patrol boats, aircraft and helicopters took part in the parade at the strategic port of Bandar Abbas overlooking the Strait of Hormuz.

State-run television, broadcasting live from the scene, showed supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, commander-in-chief of Iran's half-million strong armed forces, and military commanders taking the salute.

The Guards, protectors of the 1979 revolution which toppled the monarchy, launched 10 patrol boats equipped with Iranian-built Tondar (Thunder) missile launchers on Tuesday evening at the start of the wargames, the state news agency IRNA reported from Bandar Abbas.
More than 200,000 troops and 200 vessels of various types are involved in the three-day amphibious exercises, which are code-named "Tariq ol-Qods" (Road to Jerusalem).
They are aimed at training for surprise attacks on "enemies" threatening the Islamic Republic's security.

The Revolutionary Guards deputy commander, Brigadier-General Rahim Safavi, said the wargames were defensive in nature. They would include major amphibious exercises in the Strait of Hormuz, through which more than 15 million barrels of oil -- half the world's oil exports -- pass each day.
Troops will take part in mock battles in four provinces stretching the length of the Gulf and reaching inland to the Iraqi border.
IRNA said Khamenei was officially welcomed at the naval base in Bandar Abbas by senior military commanders.
Revolutionary Guard commander Mohsen Rezaei and chiefs of ground, air, and naval forces together with Basij militia volunteers briefed him on the manoeuvres.
Khamenei inspected the Qadr missile-launching vessel where he was briefed on its military and defence capabilities and features, IRNA said.
He also inspected an exhibition of the Revolutionary Guard naval forces displaying achievements in the areas of research and self-sufficiency including missile projects.
Tests firings of surface-to-air, shore-to-sea and surface-to-surface missiles were due to take place during the wargames.
